item.title: Japan earthquake: 23 injured after magnitude 7.5 quake; tsunami warning lifted — what we know so far
item.description: A powerful magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck off northern Japan, triggering a tsunami that hit Pacific coast communities and injured at least 23 people. Authorities warned of possible aftershocks and an increased risk of a megaquake, urging residents to remain prepared for potential evacuations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘India should not be dumping rice’: Trump signals fresh tariffs as US farmers decry cheap imports
item.description: US President Donald Trump is considering new tariffs on agricultural imports, including Indian rice and Canadian fertilizers, to support domestic farmers facing competition from cheaper foreign goods. He vowed to address alleged dumping of Indian rice and explore severe tariffs on Canadian fertilizers to boost local production, amidst ongoing trade negotiations and economic pressures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Courtroom bombshell: Bodycam shows police find loaded magazine hidden in wet underwear in Luigi Mangione’s bag
item.description: A loaded magazine, allegedly found hidden in wet underwear within Luigi Mangione's backpack, was revealed in court via body-camera footage. Mangione is accused of murdering UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. His lawyers are seeking to suppress this evidence and his statements, citing constitutional rights. Prosecutors argue the warrantless search was justified.

item.title: Texas shake-up: Jasmine Crockett enters Senate battle — is Trump critic the right pick for Democrats?
item.description: Representative Jasmine Crockett has officially launched her Texas Senate bid, aiming to challenge incumbent John Cornyn. While a strong primary favorite, her progressive stances may pose challenges in a general election. Republicans, including Cornyn and AG Ken Paxton, have already targeted Crockett, viewing her as a vulnerable opponent.

item.title: Basketball YouTuber Tristan Jass reveals he’s having brain tumor removed

Jass expressed fear but also readiness to face this challenge, receiving widespread support from fans and the online community.

item.title: Candace Owens faces fresh heat after Mark Driscoll labels her a sorceress and queen bee online as backlash grows
item.description: Pastor Mark Driscoll ignited a social media storm by calling commentator Candace Owens a "sorceress" and comparing her to a "queen bee." He is known for his direct style and strong opinions on faith and culture.

item.title: Japan struck by earthquake, tsunami: Several injuries reported, thousands advised to evacuate; what we know so far
item.description: A powerful 7.6 magnitude earthquake rocked northern Japan, triggering a tsunami of up to 70 centimeters and prompting evacuations for tens of thousands. Several injuries were reported, with fires breaking out in Aomori. Authorities have formed an emergency task force and are conducting safety checks on nuclear plants, which have shown no issues so far.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why undoing the EU combustion engine ban spooks car rentals
item.description: Europe's auto industry awaits a crucial EU announcement on December 10, potentially delaying the 2035 combustion engine phase-out amid industry pressure. Carmakers and fleet operators are pushing for concessions, citing market realities and infrastructure challenges, while the EU considers strict EV quotas for rental and leasing companies.

item.title: Unknown volcano eruption claimed as cause of Black Death
item.description: A 1345 volcanic eruption likely triggered a climate crisis, causing crop failures and forcing European port cities to open new trade routes with Central Asia. This shift, researchers suggest, inadvertently facilitated the Black Death's arrival in Europe via the bacterium Yersinia pestis. The study combines historical records with ice core and tree ring data.

item.title: Mars’ largest river systems revealed: Insights into ancient water, sediment deposits, and potential habitability for past life
item.description: Ancient Mars once teemed with flowing rivers, forming vast drainage systems. A new study has mapped these large basins, revealing they concentrated nutrients and sediments, making them prime locations for potential past life. These findings are crucial for guiding future missions in the search for evidence of ancient Martian habitability.
